## Purpose and Entry Points
Reasonix is a local, long-running coding-agent platform built around a Go engine. It is exposed through CLI/TUI, a desktop application, browser-serving mode, ACP editor integration, and bot adapters. Primary binaries are `cmd/reasonix/main.go` (CLI/ACP), `desktop/main.go` (Wails desktop host), and `cmd/e2ebench/main.go` (evaluation harness).

## Runtime Assembly and Configuration
Startup composes providers, tools, policies, extensions, session services, and runtime ownership from configuration. `internal/boot/boot.go`, `internal/boot/runtime.go`, and `internal/boot/resolver.go` are the principal composition boundary. Configuration is TOML-driven and includes provider credentials, policies, MCP, plugins, remote settings, sandboxing, and write access: `internal/config/config.go`, `internal/config/load.go`, `reasonix.example.toml`.

## Agent Turn Orchestration
The central control flow is: user/host input → control controller → agent turn loop → provider/tool events → persisted session and UI sinks. `internal/control/controller.go`, `internal/control/turn_orchestrator.go`, and `internal/agent/run_loop.go` coordinate turns, goals, pauses, approvals, retries, and finalization. The agent layer schedules tool/model work, supports planning and subagents/fleets, and applies completion/readiness gates: `internal/agent/coordinator.go`, `internal/agent/execution_engine.go`, `internal/agent/final_readiness.go`.

## Model, Tool, and Safety Boundaries
Providers are interchangeable integrations behind a common provider boundary, including OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Responses, and OpenCode paths: `internal/provider/provider.go`, `internal/provider/openai/openai.go`, `internal/provider/anthropic/anthropic.go`. Tool dispatch separates declared contracts from built-in workspace/shell operations: `internal/tool/tool.go`, `internal/agent/tool_dispatch.go`, `internal/tool/builtin/`. Write operations are guarded by permissions, workspace leases, sandbox confinement, and per-turn checkpoints: `internal/permission/permission.go`, `internal/sandbox/sandbox.go`, `internal/checkpoint/checkpoint.go`.

## Durable State, Context, and Recovery
Sessions persist event/history state with leases and write-authority controls, enabling resume, recovery, catalogs, and concurrent-host protection. Core persistence resides in `internal/agent/session.go`, `internal/agent/session_writer.go`, and `internal/sessioncatalog/catalog.go`. Context maintenance compacts/prunes conversation and tool output under provider budgets: `internal/agent/context_manager.go`, `internal/agent/compact.go`, `internal/provider/context_budget.go`. Recovery and rewind use persisted decisions and checkpoint transactions: `internal/recovery/state.go`, `internal/control/recovery.go`, `internal/control/rewind.go`.

## Host Surfaces and Protocols
CLI/TUI and browser serving are host adapters over the same engine: `internal/cli/cli.go`, `internal/cli/chat_tui.go`, `internal/serve/serve.go`. ACP provides an editor-facing server/service protocol: `internal/acp/server.go`, `internal/acp/service.go`, `internal/acp/protocol.go`. The desktop host exposes Go APIs/events to a React frontend; session, remote, and application lifecycle logic are in `desktop/app.go`, `desktop/session_runtime.go`, and `desktop/remote_app.go`, while the UI starts at `desktop/frontend/src/main.tsx` and `desktop/frontend/src/App.tsx`.

## Extensibility, Remote Operation, and Infrastructure
MCP servers and extension sidecars can add tools, providers, resources, event interception, and UI. Their protocol/runtime boundary is `internal/extension/protocol/protocol.go`, `internal/extension/sidecar/manager.go`, and `internal/plugin/plugin.go`. Remote workspaces use SSH/bootstrap/forwarding and remote filesystem support: `internal/remote/client.go`, `internal/remote/bootstrap/bootstrap.go`, `internal/remote/forward/forward.go`. External operational services include bot channels (`internal/bot/`) and Cloudflare-style workers for accounts, crash reporting, package registry, and forum functionality: `workers/accounts/src/index.ts`, `workers/crash-report/src/index.ts`, `workers/forum/src/index.ts`.
